column3: On what date did the French Foreign Office extend the invitation to the embassy in Paris?
column4: June 6, as stated by Elbrick.
column5: P01-B|On June 6 the French Foreign Office extended an invitation to our Embassy in Paris to send a representative to visit the scene of the Melouza massacre.

column3: How did Rountree's recommendation on accepting the French visit differ from Elbrick's?
column4: Rountree opposed acceptance by representatives of either office. Elbrick supported a Consulate General representative if invited and said the Paris Embassy should decline for itself.
column5: P01-A|NEA does not feel that in the framework in which the French invitation to visit the scene of the Melouza massacre has been put, representatives of either the Embassy or the Consulate General at Algiers should accept.
column6: P01-B|the Consulate General should be authorized to send a representative if an invitation is extended to the Consulate, but that the Paris Embassy should decline for itself.

column3: What did Rountree say would also need consideration if the French invitation was accepted?
column4: He said any invitation from the Arab states to participate in an international investigating commission would need serious consideration.
column5: P01-A|If, on the other hand, we decide to accept the French invitation, I believe we shall have to give serious consideration to any invitation of the Arab states to participate likewise in an international investigating commission.

column3: Who actually traveled as the American representative on the Melouza visit?
column4: Withhold. The sources give recommendations and conditions, with no confirmation of who traveled.
column5: P01-B|the Consulate General should be authorized to send a representative if an invitation is extended to the Consulate

column3: How long was each principal's opening statement allotted in the ANZUS agenda?
column4: 15–20 minutes for each principal.
column5: P02-A|Opening statements of 15–20 minutes by each principal

column3: What coordination did Hasluck seek, and what institutional limit did the later East Asian Affairs paper put on it?
column4: Hasluck wanted maximum coordination among the United States, United Kingdom, Australia, and New Zealand. The later paper kept ANZUS consultations separate from ANZAM because they serve different purposes.
column5: P02-A|he considers it essential to achieve the maximum coordination possible of the efforts of the U.S., the U.K., Australia, and New Zealand in Southeast Asia.
column6: P02-B|it is essential to keep our consultations under ANZUS separate from U.K., Australian, and New Zealand consultations under the ANZAM arrangement

column3: How certain was the scope paper that New Zealand would press for a negotiated Vietnam settlement?
column4: It forecast that New Zealand would probably emphasize a negotiated settlement, rather than recording an actual statement by New Zealand at the meeting.
column5: P02-A|will probably emphasize the desirability of pressing on to a negotiated settlement in Viet-Nam.

column3: Which of the two proposed venues was ultimately chosen for the four-party consultations?
column4: Withhold. The June 24 paper lists possible arrangements without recording a final choice.
column5: P02-B|We would be prepared to accept one of the following alternatives for quadripartite consultations on Southeast Asia:

column3: Which seven countries tabled the draft resolution that Lodge quoted?
column4: Argentina, Brazil, Cuba, Ecuador, El Salvador, Haiti, and Honduras.
column5: P03-B|by Argentina, Brazil, Cuba, Ecuador, El Salvador, Haiti and Honduras:

column3: What obligations did paragraphs 3 and 4 of the proposal quoted by Lodge introduce, and what did the Department instruct its delegation to do about them?
column4: After six months without agreement the Secretary General would appoint a person, and he was requested to report at the next regular session. The Department instructed GADel to oppose both clauses.
column5: P03-B|3. Decides that, if within the next six months the parties have not reached agreement on the suggestions made in the foregoing paragraphs, the Secretary General shall appoint a person for the purposes specified above. 4. Requests the Secretary General to report to the General Assembly at its next regular session on the results obtained.
column6: P03-A|Consequently GADel should oppose Paragraphs 3 and 4

column3: If a method for appointing a mediator could not be avoided, on what condition would the Department favor the Secretary General assisting?
column4: The parties had to consent. This was a contingent fallback if the majority insisted.
column5: P03-A|If majority insistent upon providing method for appointment mediator in event parties unable agree, we are inclined to feel this should be authorization to SYG to assist parties with their consent.

column3: What did the General Assembly ultimately decide on the draft's third and fourth paragraphs?
column4: Withhold. One cable reports a tabled draft and the other gives an instruction. The final decision is absent.
column5: P03-B|Following resolution tabled at this afternoon’s ad hoc political committee meeting
column6: P03-A|Consequently GADel should oppose Paragraphs 3 and 4

column3: At what time did the June 30 discussion at Birch Grove end?
column5: P04-B|from 11:45 a.m. until 1:15 p.m., Sunday, June 30, 1963.

column3: How does Macmillan's first preference in the July 4 letter compare with Rusk's priority in the June 30 conversation?
column4: Both preferred pursuing a comprehensive or full ban first. Rusk emphasized continuing that effort before falling back to a partial ban.
column5: P04-A|press on in the first instance to see whether accommodation can be reached to get the full ban.
column6: P04-B|Secretary Rusk emphasized the importance for pressing for a comprehensive ban for quite some time before falling back to a partial ban.

column3: Did Macmillan present his proposals as a settled position in the letter relayed by de Zulueta?
column4: No. He explicitly qualifies them as his first thoughts.
column5: P04-A|These, however, are only my first thoughts.

column3: When did Kennedy's office actually receive the original letter carried separately from the telegram?
column4: Withhold. The sender relayed the text and expected the original to arrive in due course. The packet has no actual receipt date.
column5: P04-A|I am sending you now the text of his letter of which the original will reach you in due course.

column3: What was the amount of the US loan mentioned in the April 15 memorandum?
column4: $100 million.
column5: P05-A|the U.S. loan of $100 million

column3: Did the March report and April memorandum agree about whether the United States should continue supporting the Coal and Steel Community?
column4: Yes. The March report called the policy sound and urged continuation. The April suggested position recommended no change to US support at that time.
column5: P05-B|U.S. policy toward the High Authority and the CSC itself is sound and should be continued.
column6: P05-A|No change should be made at this time in the policy of United States support for the Coal and Steel Community

column3: Did Dodge claim the existing evidence settled how effectively the High Authority was using its legal powers or the loan?
column4: No. The memo expressly describes that evidence as inconclusive and requests a study.
column5: P05-A|In view of the inconclusiveness of present evidence as to whether the High Authority is using the legal authority available to it, or is administering the U.S. loan of $100 million

column3: What were the findings of the further State Department study requested in April?
column4: Withhold. The memo requests a study and recommendations. Neither source gives its completed findings.
column5: P05-A|To submit recommendations based on the above study

column3: What date is on the response from Washington to the station in Guatemala?
column5: P06-A|Washington, June 22, 1954, 0315Z.

column3: Which numbered station telegram in this packet did the June 22 response explicitly acknowledge?
column4: It acknowledged GUAT 906, which is the June 19 telegram printed as 906. The response also mentions another telegram which is outside this pair.
column5: P06-A|particularly GUAT 906 (IN 19969) and GUAT 919 (IN 20161).

column3: How certain did the June 22 writer say he was about the judgment discussed in that paragraph?
column4: The writer expressly allows that their judgment might have been right or wrong.
column5: P06-A|Here our judgment may or may not have been correct

column3: What was the full text of the other station message numbered GUAT 919?
column4: Withhold. The later cable identifies it but this packet gives only the text of GUAT 906.
column5: P06-A|particularly GUAT 906 (IN 19969) and GUAT 919 (IN 20161).
